title: When school funding records were missing, what could auditors still verify?

beats.text: School auditors found 6.30 units of attendance without supporting records.

visual.sub: Missing attendance records did not result in a state funding claim

beats.text: The district had caught them before reporting, and claimed no state funding.
The next audit marked the attendance finding resolved.

visual.kicker: Missing attendance records did not result in a state funding claim

beats.text: A different audit tested spending from a state pandemic grant.

visual.kicker: Auditors could not verify spending before in-person instruction

beats.text: The district did not provide the spending needed to test the 15 percent limit.

visual.kicker: Auditors could not verify spending before in-person instruction

beats.text: Its board-approved plan showed planned spending, with actual figures still to come.
Auditors called the filing late. The fifth calendar day fell on Sunday.

visual.kicker: Auditors could not verify spending before in-person instruction

beats.text: The district submitted it the next day, Memorial Day.

visual.kicker: Auditors could not verify spending before in-person instruction

beats.text: In fiscal 2022, child-care auditors could not obtain the district’s recovery procedures.

visual.kicker: The district could not produce child-care recovery procedures

beats.text: They reported no known fraudulent payments or questioned costs.

visual.kicker: The district could not produce child-care recovery procedures

beats.text: For federal salaries, two of 60 employees lacked time certifications.
Other payroll records established that both salary charges were allowable.

visual.kicker: Alternative payroll records supported two federal salary charges

beats.text: The following audit marked the certification recommendation implemented.
Every source is linked in the case file below.
